title: Frontend security hardening: HTTPS redirect, asset headers, validation, CSRF wiring, and friendly error pages

requirements.summary: Force HTTPS via client-side redirect on initial app load while preserving path/query/hash and skipping local development hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: When visiting any app route over http://, the browser is redirected to the equivalent https:// URL with the same path/search/hash.
The redirect does not run during local development (e.g., localhost) to avoid breaking dev workflows.
The redirect does not create an infinite redirect loop.

file_operations.description: Add a small utility that checks window.location (protocol/host) and performs a one-time replace() redirect from http: to https: while preserving pathname, search, and hash; ensure localhost/127.0.0.1 (and typical dev hostnames) are excluded to avoid breaking dev workflows.

Invoke the HTTPS enforcement utility before React renders so deep links redirect immediately and consistently; ensure this runs only in the browser (not during SSR) and does not execute when already on https:.

requirements.summary: Add standard security headers for the frontend asset canister via .ic-assets.json5, including a restrictive CSP that preserves required app functionality (fonts/II/etc.).
acceptanceCriteria: `index.html` responses include the configured security headers after deployment.
Security headers do not break required app functionality (React app loads, Internet Identity sign-in works, fonts/icons load as expected).
CSP is explicitly defined and is not left as an empty/placeholder policy.

file_operations.description: Extend the asset rules to attach security headers (at minimum Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and an explicit restrictive Content-Security-Policy) for index.html and other relevant served assets; ensure CSP allows required sources used by this app (e.g., self-hosted assets, Google Fonts domains referenced in frontend/index.html, and any required IC/Internet Identity connections) without being a placeholder.

Review and, if necessary, adjust external resource usage (e.g., font links) so the configured CSP in frontend/public/.ic-assets.json5 can remain restrictive without breaking app load or sign-in flows (do not add new third-party resources unless required).

requirements.summary: Add frontend input normalization and validation (trim/max length/pattern checks) for user-controlled fields before submission, with clear inline messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend rejects invalid or unexpectedly large payloads with clear error messages and does not write partial/dirty data to state.
Frontend form fields display user-friendly validation messages in English before submission for common invalid inputs (e.g., empty required fields, invalid ZIP/DOB).
All stored text fields are normalized (e.g., trimmed) consistently.

file_operations.description: Create shared frontend validators/normalizers for common fields used in orders (trim, max lengths, allowed character sets; structured validation for DOB, ZIP, state/state_name normalization, gender, height, and ID/order IDs) to ensure consistent sanitization across forms before invoking backend calls.

Update form validation to use the shared validation utilities: enforce max lengths and patterns (e.g., ZIP format, reasonable name/address characters), ensure state/state_name values are normalized consistently, and show clear InlineFieldMessage errors for invalid inputs prior to submission; normalize all strings (trim) before creating the payload.

Normalize and validate create-order payload right before the backend call (defense-in-depth): trim strings, enforce max lengths, and reject invalid structured fields with clear thrown errors so the UI can display a friendly message.

Add basic tracking number validation/normalization (trim, length limits, allowed characters) before calling the backend so admin updates fail fast with readable errors rather than sending malformed input.

requirements.summary: Wire a CSRF token flow in the frontend so all mutating backend calls include a caller-scoped token once the backend capability is available.
acceptanceCriteria: Mutating operations invoked from the frontend include a CSRF token parameter and the backend validates it before applying changes.
CSRF tokens are caller-scoped and cannot be reused across different principals.
If the CSRF token is missing/invalid, the backend denies the request without mutating state and returns a clear error/trap message.

file_operations.description: Add a small hook that retrieves and caches a CSRF token per authenticated session/caller (and clears it on logout via existing auth clearing behavior); implement refresh/retry behavior suitable for token invalidation. This hook should be designed to call a backend capability for minting/returning a token once it exists.

Update the order creation mutation to obtain a CSRF token via the new hook and include it with the state-changing backend call once the backend capability supports it; ensure missing/invalid token errors are surfaced to the user as readable messages.
Update delete-order mutation to include a CSRF token from the CSRF hook when calling the state-changing backend function; handle token errors gracefully and avoid retry loops that could spam calls.
Update order-status mutation to include a CSRF token parameter (via CSRF hook) for state changes; surface authorization/CSRF failures with clear UI errors.
Update tracking-number mutation to include CSRF token; ensure token acquisition is performed only when an actor is available and the user is authenticated.

Update all security/admin state-changing mutations (toggle security, update rate limits, clear counters, allow/block list mutations) to include CSRF token support through the CSRF hook so admin operations are protected consistently once the backend capability is present.

requirements.summary: Add friendly 404 and 500 error pages integrated with TanStack Router not-found and error handling and matching the existing AppShell layout.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to an unknown route shows a dedicated 404 page (not a blank screen).
A thrown route/component error renders a friendly 500-style error page with clear English copy and a navigation option to recover (e.g., go home).
Error pages match the site’s existing layout shell (header/footer) and remain accessible (proper headings, readable contrast, keyboard reachable links/buttons).

file_operations.description: Create a dedicated, friendly Not Found (404) page with accessible headings and a clear recovery action (e.g., button to go to / or /dashboard depending on auth), styled to match the current UI patterns (cards/buttons) and intended to render within AppShell.

Create a generic friendly Error (500-style) page component for unexpected route/app errors with clear English guidance, optional error details for debugging (non-sensitive), and a primary recovery navigation action; ensure keyboard accessible controls and readable contrast.

Wire TanStack Router not-found and error handling to render the new NotFoundPage and ErrorPage (root route notFoundComponent/errorComponent or equivalent), ensuring these pages render inside the existing Layout/AppShell and are reachable for unknown routes and thrown route/component errors.
